title: 48-hour railway strike begins
byline: Sri Lanka’s railway trade unions launched a 48-hour token strike at midnight yesterday (16), after talks with the Government failed to resolve their demand for the removal of Railway General Manager Ravindra Pathmapriya.

title: Australia to bar foreign students from bringing partners, children while they study
byline: Australia will stop foreign students from bringing their partners and children to accompany them while they study and tighten rules for temporary migrants ​to switch visas, media reported on Thursday, ahead of a minister’s ‌speech on immigration changes.

title: 1,665 schools operate with fewer than 50 students each
byline: In the wake of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s remarks on the plan for restructuring the school system, statistics reveal that 1,665 schools, including one national school, operate with fewer than 50 students each.

title: Australia cracks down on student and backpacker visas to curb migration
byline: Australia will stop foreign students from bringing partners and children to ​accompany them while they study and tighten working holiday visa rules, a senior minister said on Thursday, amid growing debate ‌over high migration levels.

title: SLPP member Renuka Perera arrested
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) member and former National Transport Commission (NTC) Chairman Renuka Perera over corruption allegations involving bus permits for the Southern Expressway.

title: Mattakkuliya crash: Driver was under cannabis influence- police
byline: Police have found that the driver arrested in connection with the fatal multi-vehicle accident in Mattakkuliya yesterday was driving under the influence of cannabis at the time of the crash.

title: Shiranthi Rajapaksa admitted to Mount Elizabeth Hospital in Singapore
byline: Shiranthi Rajapaksa, wife of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, who left the country yesterday morning, is presently in Singapore undergoing a medical check-up at the elite Mount Elizabeth Hospital, sources told the Daily Mirror last evening.

title: Fiji declares HIV a national emergency as cases surge
byline: Fiji has declared a national emergency as HIV cases surge, and is expanding access to testing, treatment and prevention services.

title: Pre-trial conference fixed in corruption case against Karannagoda, Yoshitha
byline: A corruption case filed by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) against former Sri Lanka Navy Commander Admiral of the Fleet Wasantha Karannagoda and Yoshitha Rajapaksa was taken up before the Colombo High Court today, with the court fixing the case for a pre-trial conference.

title: Court Assistant arrested over Rs. 500 bribe
byline: An Office Assistant attached to the Fort Magistrate’s Court has been arrested by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) for allegedly soliciting and accepting a bribe of Rs. 500.

title: New rabies law ends arbitrary killing of animals on suspicion, veterinarian says
byline: Animals suspected of having rabies can no longer be arbitrarily killed or shot by police merely on suspicion under Sri Lanka’s newly introduced legislation on rabies control and dog registration, Veterinary Surgeon and Animal Welfare Coalition (AWC) Executive Member Dr. Chamith Nanayakkara said.

title: Leopard cub rescued after wandering into house in Bulathkohupitiya
byline: A well-grown leopard cub that had wandered into a house in Dedugala, Bulathkohupitiya, was safely rescued by wildlife officials following a coordinated operation.

title: The Opposition: NPP’s greatest asset
byline: One wonders whether the public rally organised by the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) with massive publicity in Anuradhapura last Saturday — intended to create a favorable political wave across the country — has instead turned into a political disaster for the party itself.

title: Actor Vishwa Kodikara fined Rs. 5,000 over cocaine possession
byline: Film and teledrama actor Vishwa Kodikara was fined Rs. 5,000 by Mount Lavinia Magistrate Kanchana Neranjala Silva after he pleaded guilty to possessing cocaine.

title: Warrants issued on Aravinda de Silva, his wife recalled
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena today ordered the recall of warrants issued yesterday on former Sri Lankan cricketer Aravinda de Silva and his wife, who had stood as sureties for the wife of Kapila Chandrasena, a suspect in the alleged payment of a USD 2 million bribe in connection with the purchase of Airbus aircraft by SriLankan Airlines.

title: Sonal Dinusha named ICC Men’s Player of the Month
byline: Sonal Dinusha has been named the ICC Men’s Player of the Month for August 2026.

title: Universities have moral responsibility to curb ragging: PM
byline: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya has stressed that universities have a moral responsibility to prevent and control ragging and ensure that students subjected to such incidents have confidence in the investigative procedures in place.

title: Parliamentary Committee approves petroleum exploration bidding process
byline: The Ministerial Consultative Committee on Energy Affairs has approved the Order governing the calling for investment proposals for the exploration and development of petroleum resources in Sri Lanka.

title: JR’s grandson recalls grandfather’s stand on corruption
byline: Pradeep Jayewardene, grandson of late President J.R. Jayewardene, recalled his grandfather’s stance on corruption, saying that people should not accuse others of corruption as there could be corrupt individuals within their own camp.

title: CSE extends four-day slide as ASPI nears 21,000
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange closed lower for a fourth consecutive session on 17 September 2026, with both benchmark indices weakening amid sustained selling pressure and cautious investor sentiment.

title: Prison officers’ salaries, allowances to get attention in Budget: Minister
byline: The Government is considering increasing the salaries and allowances of prison officers in the upcoming Budget, Minister of Justice and National Integration Harshana Nanayakkara said.

title: Sri Lanka, Thailand expedite visa-free travel talks
byline: Sri Lanka and Thailand have agreed to further strengthen bilateral relations, with both sides discussing steps to expedite arrangements for visa exemption for holders of ordinary passports.

title: Three-wheeler driver dies after Dematagoda shooting
byline: A three-wheeler driver who was injured in a shooting incident near the ‘Kalu Palama’ in Dematagoda this evening has succumbed to his injuries while receiving treatment in hospital, police said.

title: Five businesses fined over defective diapers
byline: Five businesses have been fined a total of Rs.140,000 after being found selling and distributing baby and adult diapers without the required importer details, following complaints from consumers that some diapers deteriorated and tore during use.

title: “I’m a Tiger but not an LTTE Tiger” - Archchuna
byline: Jaffna District MP Ramanathan Archchuna defended his use of the word “tiger”, saying he would not consider it an offence to identify himself with the animal, while denying that he had referred to a “Tiger diaspora”.

title: Pakistan announces austerity measures to conserve fuel as Gulf conflict spirals
byline: Pakistan announced on Thursday a cut in fuel for official vehicles, bans on ​vehicle purchases by the state, foreign visits by ‌officials, and official dinners, as part of a slew of austerity measures in a bid to conserve energy as fuel prices spike ​due to the Gulf conflict.

title: Sri Lanka’s first battery storage, floating solar plant to open tomorrow
byline: Sri Lanka’s first Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), aimed at strengthening renewable energy capacity and improving the stability of the national electricity grid, will be inaugurated tomorrow (18) in Anuradhapura.
